terms.gloss: bear, yield (of land, trees, a country)
evidence: Cic. Leg. 2.67: quae autem terra frūgēs ferre … possit
Ov. Met. 1.109: frūgēs tellūs inarāta ferēbat
terms.comment: The land or the tree is the subject: ager frūmentum fert; a fertile field is ferāx. Of people making goods, Latin says facere (see make).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.48: agrōs fertilēs, quī multō plūs efferunt quam accēpērunt

terms.gloss: produce (of a land, the sea, nature)
evidence: Tac. Agr. 12.6: gignit et Ōceanus margarīta
Sen. Ep. 18.14: immodica īra gignit īnsāniam
Cic. N. D. 1.4: frūgēs et reliqua, quae terra pariat
Ov. Ars 1.757: nec tellūs eadem parit omnia
terms.comment: Properly of giving birth; also of the earth bringing forth crops.

phrases.latin: mox etiam frūgēs tellūs inarāta ferēbat
phrases.english: soon the earth, unploughed, produced crops as well

phrases.latin: an imitārī agrōs fertilēs, quī multō plūs efferunt quam accēpērunt?
phrases.english: or should we copy fertile fields, which produce far more than they received?

phrases.latin: nec tellūs eadem parit omnia; vītibus illa convenit, haec oleīs; hāc bene farra virent
phrases.english: nor does the same soil produce everything: one suits vines, another olives; in this one the wheat grows green
